sections_en.text: This document covers the half-yearly maintenance of 400 V motors. The document was prepared by Eng. Mohamed Salim Salman and Eng. Sami Mohamed Hassan, and the electronic correspondence was carried out over the Internet with the assistance of Eng. Mohamed Salim Salman.

It was implemented based on previous experience by Eng. Saeed Abdel Maqsoud Awad Allah on 1/10/2001. The document was reviewed by Eng. Abouda El-Banna, Inspection and Quality Control Engineer, and Eng. Mohamed El-Sayed Abdel Ghaffar, General Manager of the station, and approved by Eng. Awad Mohamed Fathy, Head of the Power Stations Sector.

items: Issue an approved work order from the competent authority, stating the industrial safety category
Switch off the motor switch and withdraw it to the test position.
Isolate the motor from the pump mechanically.
Wear personal protective equipment (coveralls, helmet, safety shoes).
Screwdrivers of different sizes
Avometer.
Open-end wrench set

sections_en.text: Work steps to be carried out

items: Disconnect the motor terminals and measure the winding resistance with the avometer between the phases, and between the phases and earth, and record (S-T) & (R-T) & (R-S) & (R-E) & (S-E) & (T-E).
Make sure the motor terminal box is sound and has no breakdown or breakage; if any is found, the terminal box must be replaced.
Check the serviceability of the motor ball bearings.
Put oil in the gearbox of the motor through the specialised maintenance department.
Tighten the motor and cable terminals well to the terminal box.
Test the motor on no-load before connecting the gear coupling, and measure the current on the three phases and compare the no-load current shown on the nameplate on the motor, using the clamp meter.
Close the terminal box tightly to prevent any water leaking inside.
Close the work order, clear the site, and hand over the condition to the responsible operating engineer.

Egyptian Electricity Holding Company
Maintenance Procedure Information System
Maintenance Procedure Information System
 | Transformer Stations | Maintenance Procedures
Document No.:
M-000-M6-r0a | Equipment: 400 V motors
Issued to: El-Arish Steam Power Station
Status: First draft
Publication Date: | Procedure: Half-yearly inspection and maintenance
Next Review Date:
Introduction
This document covers the half-yearly maintenance of 400 V motors. The document was prepared by Eng. Mohamed Salim Salman and Eng. Sami Mohamed Hassan, and the electronic correspondence was carried out over the Internet with the assistance of Eng. Mohamed Salim Salman.
It was implemented based on previous experience by Eng. Saeed Abdel Maqsoud Awad Allah on 1/10/2001. The document was reviewed by Eng. Abouda El-Banna, Inspection and Quality Control Engineer, and Eng. Mohamed El-Sayed Abdel Ghaffar, General Manager of the station, and approved by Eng. Awad Mohamed Fathy, Head of the Power Stations Sector.
Safety precautions
Issue an approved work order from the competent authority, stating the industrial safety category
Switch off the motor switch and withdraw it to the test position.
Isolate the motor from the pump mechanically.
Wear personal protective equipment (coveralls, helmet, safety shoes).
Tools, instruments and equipment used
Screwdrivers of different sizes
Avometer.
Open-end wrench set
Work steps to be carried out
Disconnect the motor terminals and measure the winding resistance with the avometer between the phases, and between the phases and earth, and record (S-T) & (R-T) & (R-S) & (R-E) & (S-E) & (T-E).
Make sure the motor terminal box is sound and has no breakdown or breakage; if any is found, the terminal box must be replaced.
Check the serviceability of the motor ball bearings.
Put oil in the gearbox of the motor through the specialised maintenance department.
Tighten the motor and cable terminals well to the terminal box.
Test the motor on no-load before connecting the gear coupling, and measure the current on the three phases and compare the no-load current shown on the nameplate on the motor, using the clamp meter.
Close the terminal box tightly to prevent any water leaking inside.
Close the work order, clear the site, and hand over the condition to the responsible operating engineer.
